name: Centrist populism
summary: Centrist populism is a style of anti-establishment politics, found mostly in Central and Eastern Europe, that attacks corrupt and unresponsive mainstream parties in the name of ordinary people without committing to a left or right ideology. It is personalistic, usually led by outsider entrepreneurs or celebrities, stresses competence, probity and rising living standards, and accepts the market economy and existing welfare systems. It criticises liberal-democratic checks only moderately and is less nationalist and less nativist than right-wing populism.
scope: The profile represents the CEE-centred family described by Smilov, Enyedi, Hanley and Sikk, Stanley and others: Simeon II's NDSV, GERB, Czech ANO 2011, Public Affairs, Res Publica, New Era, OLaNO and similar anti-establishment reform parties, with Macron's En Marche as a looser pro-EU relative. It excludes parties that became right-wing populist (Fidesz and PiS after their shift) and the well-defined thick-ideology populisms. Because the family avoids doctrine, most statements outside corruption, democracy and economics are inferred, low-confidence answers.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Centrist populists keep existing welfare systems and avoid welfare retrenchment, so an adherent would back state-guaranteed health care without making it a cause.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Their emphasis on rising living standards and retained welfare protection suggests mild support for wage floors, though sources give no explicit wage platform.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The sources describe these parties as accepting the market economy and lacking anti-capitalism, while stressing state competence rather than laissez-faire dogma.

public-ownership.rationale: Not anti-capitalist and favouring business-style management of the state, they are unlikely to push nationalising utilities; inferred from market acceptance.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Economic policy is deliberately blurred (valence populism) and ANO-type parties mix business-friendly and centre-left tax measures, so adherents split.

unions-good.rationale: These parties avoid class-based economic positions, and the sources record no stance on organised labour.

property-fundamental.rationale: Accepting the market economy implies respect for property, but the sources record no explicit rights doctrine; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anti-establishment parties attack corrupt links between business and politics, yet business-run entrepreneurs lead several of them; adherents are split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Centrist populists are described as less given to welfare chauvinism and as wanting to keep existing welfare systems, so cutting welfare as dependency-creating is not their line.

worker-ownership.rationale: Lacking anti-capitalism and class politics, they have no interest in collective worker ownership; inferred from their market acceptance.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No documented stance; the movements focus on probity and competence rather than security policy, so neutral.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Socio-cultural issues are avoided by valence-style populists, so no consistent position on drug policy.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The sources show no position; these parties steer clear of culture-war questions.

strong-leader.rationale: Centrist populism is personalistic and led by charismatic political entrepreneurs who promise to cut through the establishment, so a decisive leader is welcome, though most do not reject pluralism.

state-harmful.rationale: They want a competent, honest and cleaned-up state, not its abolition; critique is aimed at corruption and the establishment, not at the state as such.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented position; gun control is not among the valence issues these parties campaign on.

empower-police-military.rationale: The sources record no security platform; focus is on anti-corruption and competence.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: A socio-cultural issue these parties generally avoid taking stands on.

decide-locally.rationale: Sources mention recall and direct democracy but no consistent decentralisation stance; some like ANO are centralised in organisation.

rehabilitation.rationale: No documented stance on penal policy; adherents are not united.

traditional-family.rationale: Described as not strongly culturally conservative nor liberal, so an adherent is neutral on this.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Centrist populists avoid socio-cultural positions and the family includes parties of differing leanings; neutral inference.

abortion-legal.rationale: These parties avoid moral-cultural issues, and the sources record no stance.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not culturally conservative according to the sources, and technocratic in style, so a larger public role for religion is unlikely to be pushed; inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a concern in the sources; centrist populists typically avoid identity politics.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No documented position; outside their valence-issue agenda.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Sources call them not strongly nationalist yet sometimes mildly nationalistic, so mild agreement is inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: They present themselves as reformers breaking with an ossified party establishment, so they favour sweeping renewal over deference to established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The sources do not address immigration directly; centrist populists are contrasted with right-wing populists who campaign on it.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Described as less supportive of the EU and anti-bureaucratic about supranational technocracy, but not anti-Western.

free-trade.rationale: Accepting the market economy and pro-growth, but no explicit trade doctrine in the sources; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Mildly nationalistic at most, but Macron-type centrists are pro-European; the family is split.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign policy is not part of their documented agenda.

open-borders.rationale: Not a stated aim; moderate centrists generally keep borders, and welfare chauvinism is absent, so mild disagreement is inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Their appeal rests on rising living standards and economic good times, so limiting growth contradicts their emphasis.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Valence populism is sometimes linked to climate scepticism while Macron-style centrists back climate action; split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No documented stance; technocratic strands favour technical solutions but make no grand claim.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No documented stance on energy policy.

revolution-justified.rationale: They are non-extremist, work within elections to renew politics and do not reject pluralism, so revolution is outside their approach.

experts-over-public.rationale: Technocratic strands such as Czech ANO favour expert-run, business-style government and emphasise competence, though populist rhetoric also invokes the people; mild agreement.

central-planning.rationale: They accept the market economy and lack anti-capitalist elements, so a planned economy is excluded.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not a topic in the sources; ownership forms are not a concern for parties without economic ideology.

land-value-tax.rationale: Specific tax doctrines are absent from the sources.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No documented stance; economic policy is blurred.

basic-income.rationale: They keep existing welfare systems rather than propose radical new ones, and stress competence over redistribution experiments; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Market-accepting and pro-EU-single-market in many cases; no protectionist doctrine in the sources.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Business-style technocrats might favour targeted investment (Macron's programme speaks of targeted investment), yet the sources give no clear line.

widespread-small-property.rationale: No documented position on property distribution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing money wages is incompatible with the accepted market economy of centrist populists.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A pro-market but mainstream-institutional movement; abolishing central banks is a libertarian fringe idea absent from the sources.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: No sign of corporatism in the sources; they criticise established bodies rather than build state-recognised ones.

one-party-rule.rationale: They compete in elections and are said not to reject political pluralism or challenge liberal democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Mostly irrelevant, though Bulgaria's Simeon II movement was led by a former monarch; no consistent view.

democracy-best.rationale: Scholars cited argue these parties moderately criticise but do not challenge liberal democracy or pluralism, so they affirm democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Some centrist populist parties promote direct democracy, consistent with the claim to speak for the people against party elites.

workers-councils.rationale: Class-based councils are alien to a non-ideological movement that works through parliaments.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not discussed; moderate, not strongly nationalist parties generally defend state unity.

natural-rulers.rationale: They attack established elites and claim to speak for ordinary people, but admit non-politician entrepreneurs; mild disagreement.

political-violence-never.rationale: Described as non-extremist; inferred rejection of political violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Moderate and non-militarist in documented form; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; they avoid cultural-religious issues.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Non-ideological, technocratic and not culturally conservative, so scripture-based law is far from their style.

private-courts-defense.rationale: They want a competent state, not private substitutes for core functions; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not strongly nationalist, avoid welfare chauvinism and exclusionary nativism that marks right-wing populists.

class-struggle-history.rationale: They lack class-based ideology and reject socio-economic dogma, concentrating on competence and corruption.

equal-outcomes.rationale: No egalitarian programme is documented, and economic positions are blurred; mild disagreement inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not relevant to their documented concerns.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not anti-Western and not nationalist-expansive; no such unions in their agenda.

self-interest-moral.rationale: No philosophy of this kind; they are pragmatic.

duties-before-rights.rationale: No stated view; moderately critical of liberal democracy but not communitarian by doctrine.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is not in the sources.

limit-population.rationale: No documented stance; pro-growth, pro-welfare orientation makes active limits unlikely.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Their appeal rests on rising living standards and economic growth, the opposite of this view.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No documented stance; technocratic style is not equal to accelerationism.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Technocratic populism leans on expert decision-making, but no source ties these parties to algorithmic governance.

restore-past-order.rationale: They promise renewal and reform and are not culturally conservative, so restoration is not the aim.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Centrist populists claim to be non-ideological and judge themselves on competence, probity and results; Stanley's description of 'non-political' politics and the valence-populism definition rest on this.

direct-action.rationale: They contest elections and enter government and are not extremist, so they seek change through electoral politics.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contradicts their growth and living-standards emphasis.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Incompatible with their accepted market economy and technocratic competence.

distribute-by-need.rationale: No communist elements; inferred from absence of anti-capitalism.

production-for-use.rationale: Not anti-capitalist, accept profit-making enterprise (several leaders are entrepreneurs).

profit-exploitation.rationale: Business-founded parties such as ANO and market-accepting movements do not hold that profit is exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Pluralist, non-extremist and class-free in outlook.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not anti-capitalist; they hold no such theory.

taxation-theft.rationale: They want the state to run better, not to be minimised, and keep welfare systems funded by taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Not stated; they avoid doctrinal liberal positions.

individual-rights-only.rationale: No doctrinal stance on group rights.

exit-over-voice.rationale: They emphasise voting out the establishment, so the vote retains importance for them.

state-as-business.rationale: Czech ANO's slogan was to run the state like a firm, and technocratic centrist populists present business-model government as their remedy; though the 'citizens as customers who can leave' clause is not documented.

positive-liberty.rationale: A philosophical question not addressed by these parties.

media-academia-power.rationale: They attack political establishments rather than media or universities; no source ties them to this claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: They lack the racism of far-right outsider parties according to Hanley and Sikk.

organic-representation.rationale: They operate through parties and elections, albeit personalistic ones.

total-state.rationale: Pluralist and market-accepting; no sign of totalitarian aims.

national-rebirth.rationale: They promise renewal of politics, but a nationalist 'decadence' narrative is not documented; mildly nationalistic at most.

territorial-expansion.rationale: No expansionist content; not strongly nationalist.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Modern electoral parties; the idea is alien.

bound-labor.rationale: Legally bound agricultural labour is plainly outside a market-accepting, pluralist family that is described as non-extremist.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Technocratic and results-oriented strands assume practical, checkable competence.

single-common-good.rationale: Technocratic populism assumes single correct solutions, yet valence populism is pragmatic and disinterested in doctrine; split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not discussed in the sources on centrist populism; neutral.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not part of the documented agenda; adherents have no common line.

workplace-democracy.rationale: No workplace-democracy element in these business-friendly movements.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: ANO-style parties are cautious on budgets while Macron-style programmes favour targeted investment; no shared line.

economic-freedom.rationale: Acceptance of the market economy suggests mild agreement though no doctrinal statement is documented.

rule-by-example.rationale: Personalistic leadership trades on leaders' probity, yet no doctrine replaces laws with example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Mildly nationalistic at most and sovereignty-sensitive on the EU; the principle itself is not contested.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not an issue in the sources.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Centrist populists are less likely than right-wing populists to use welfare chauvinism. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare-conditionality is not documented; they preserve existing systems but are pro-work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Not class-conflict oriented and focused on shared living standards, so partnership is more natural.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Futurism is not part of their anti-corruption renewal programme.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not culturally conservative; no such position documented.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Hanley and Sikk distinguish these parties from far-right outsiders by their lack of racism; segregation law is not part of their agenda.

state-class-instrument.rationale: They deny class-based analysis; they criticise corrupt establishments rather than a ruling class.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration not addressed in the sources and they are contrasted with nativist parties.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy of this kind belongs to the far right, which the sources distinguish them from.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The defining feature stated by Wikipedia and by Hanley and Sikk is anti-corruption, anti-establishment rhetoric aimed at mainstream parties seen as unrepresentative.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is far from their agenda and from non-extremist, pluralist politics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not documented; they stress probity but have no stated position on past abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: They keep welfare systems and market acceptance is not minarchism.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Hanley and Sikk contrast these parties with far-right outsiders by their lack of racism, so discouraging mixed marriage is not part of their agenda.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Moderate, pluralist and not racist; no explicit statement, so inferred.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Debates about settler colonialism fall outside what these parties address.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not relevant to their documented agenda.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A South Asian religious-politics issue, absent from centrist populist documentation.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion is not in their documented agenda.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist-state doctrine is alien to them.

consent-of-governed.rationale: They promise to restore the will of the people against unrepresentative parties and remain within liberal democracy.

population-transfer.rationale: Non-extremist and without nativism; such measures belong to the far right.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Libertarian principle not addressed; they reject political violence but are not absolutists.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: No documented stance; they oppose extremism but are pluralist.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican theory not addressed, though anti-establishment critique echoes concern about unaccountable elites.

separated-powers.rationale: Wikipedia records that centrist populists criticise separation of powers and independent bodies, though they do not reject pluralism.

vanguard-party.rationale: Revolutionary vanguard parties are alien to them.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Redistribution is not a documented focus.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: No such theory; they blame corruption and establishments for failures.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed; they avoid nativist arguments.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: They want better elected leaders rather than lottery; some personalistic parties dismiss institutions, but lotteries are not documented.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Moderate; though they criticise rule-of-law constraints, they are not authoritarian by doctrine.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls on food are not documented; economic policy is deliberately blurred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Pluralist and compatible with liberal democracy; control of media is not part of this family.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not a one-party or communist family.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Anti-elite rhetoric might support curbing politicians' privileges, yet nothing is documented on pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Centrist populist parties are leader-centred and centralised (ANO's chair and bureau), but no doctrine is stated.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Wikipedia notes centrist populists tend to be less supportive of the EU, though they are not anti-Western; Macron's En Marche is a pro-EU counterexample.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Presidential versus parliamentary command of the army is not part of the documented platforms.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is irrelevant to these secular, non-ideological parties.

clerical-rule.rationale: Technocratic and non-ideological secular politics, not clerical.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist position alien to centrist populism.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Anti-establishment and pro-accountability stance suggests mild preference for term limits, though personalistic leaders resist them; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Wikipedia says some centrist populist parties promote direct democracy or recall elections.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not anti-Western; they do not call for withdrawal from alliances.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: No documented romanticism of the countryside; the parties focus on probity and competence.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification of divided nations is not discussed in the sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: They target political elites, not universities specifically; technocrats claim expertise.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not a stated theme; they are described as neither nationalist nor culturally liberal.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Cultural issues avoided by these parties.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Technocratic and not religious conservative; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Moral regulation of media is not part of their valence-issue platforms.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship law is not covered in the sources; they are contrasted with nativist parties but not set against descent rules.

minority-language-support.rationale: Minority language policy is not documented for this family.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious exemptions from general law are not a documented concern.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A Millian view of custom and conformity is not documented for these parties.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Market-accepting, mainstream fiscal attitudes; no debt-relief doctrine.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-capitalist framing is absent in this family.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not documented, though renewal rhetoric might welcome it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: They stay within liberal democracy, even if moderately critical.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global aid duties are not addressed in the sources.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear doctrine is not documented; most of these parties are in small or mid-sized states under alliances.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Anti-establishment parties often like direct election, but no source states it.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Their criticism of independent bodies may extend to central banks but is not documented, while Macron-style centrists back them.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions are not a documented concern of this family.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: No documented stance on the social function of property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate among Marxists that these parties do not enter.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation philosophy is not documented; valence populists are sometimes linked to climate scepticism, so adherents split.

collective-defense.rationale: Not anti-Western; alliances such as NATO are not rejected.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: International-law questions on annexation are not documented in the sources.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state conflict is not on their agenda.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of the head of state is not discussed; the personalistic party leaders are partisan by nature.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secession is not addressed in the sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Incompatible with a secular, democratic anti-establishment family.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not documented, though some CEE centrists adopted flat taxes; the family has no shared view.

character-from-environment.rationale: A nature-nurture question outside their political platforms.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Anti-corruption and probity rhetoric opposes rulers who place themselves above the law, whatever their stance on independent bodies.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not part of their agenda.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not engaged by these parties.

leader-cult.rationale: Personalistic leadership exists, but public leader cults are not documented.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy is not documented for them.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not discussed in the sources on centrist populism.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not strongly nationalist; irredentism is not a feature in the sources.

common-currency.rationale: Attitudes split between Macron-type pro-euro centrists and ANO's euro scepticism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government is not documented.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A debate about diaspora strategy that the parties do not address.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist theory is outside their frame.

ban-cartels.rationale: Anti-corruption and anti-establishment appeals fit competition enforcement against entrenched interests; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not documented, and anti-establishment appeals pull both ways, so adherents split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Wikipedia says centrist populists criticise the rule of law and independent bodies, yet scholars hold they do not challenge liberal democracy, so adherents split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not documented; Macron-style centrists favour parity while others avoid the issue.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs contradict accepted market economy and growth focus.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Standards in trade agreements are not documented; Macron-style pro-EU centrists might agree, others not.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not part of a market-accepting movement.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hereditary titles are marginal to their concerns, though anti-elite rhetoric hints at mild agreement.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Mildly nationalistic at most; no documented education stance.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Not part of their ideas and not nativist.

patriotic-education.rationale: Patriotic schooling is not documented; they are mildly nationalistic at most.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Accepting the market economy, they do not expect collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial influence is not a documented theme.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian view not documented; moderate centrists reject it.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Their criticism of independent bodies and rule of law limits enthusiasm for entrenchment, but they are not anti-liberal.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial-treaty questions are not documented in the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: They contest elections; leadership by election is assumed.

minority-veto.rationale: Majoritarian populist rhetoric about the people implies disagreement.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not documented, although anti-corruption fits rhetorically.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary supremacy is not stated; adherents differ given their criticism of separation of powers.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics are not part of their documented agenda.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal-use policy is not documented for this family.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: An aristocratic duty idea not found in these parties' sources.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: They mobilise citizens to participate and vote for renewal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marxist cultural critique not in frame.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian view not in their frame.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for native-born citizens is nativist, and the sources set these parties apart from nativist politics.

party-own-road.rationale: A question internal to communism, which centrist populists do not engage with.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development policy for poor countries is not documented for them.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Mild nationalism is not irredentist per scholars.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous political leadership is not documented for these parties.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional founding values are not documented; the parties are not defined by historical-memory politics.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not documented; Central European centrists often agree but sources silent.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US history dispute that is not part of their agenda.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument politics are not documented in the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-policy questions are avoided by these parties.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Gender-policy questions are avoided by these parties.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages for domestic work are not part of their platforms.

filial-duty.rationale: Family duties are not documented; they are not strongly culturally conservative.

office-by-exam.rationale: Technocratic strands prize competence over patronage; Czech ANO is described as technocratic, though not an examination doctrine.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Strategic-industry protection is not documented; they accept markets but some are sovereignty-minded.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is a cultural issue these parties avoid.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Recall elections are promoted by some, but binding mandates are not documented.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Contradicts market acceptance and property systems.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Pluralist, within liberal democracy; basic parliamentary control assumed.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not documented for this family.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign land ownership is not documented in the sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Their focus on rising living standards cuts against it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert foreign policy is not addressed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-establishment critique of links between business and politicians suggests mild agreement, though business founders lead some parties.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Fidesz and PiS in their later phases did, but the family is split.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy is not documented; they are not defined by immigration stances.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property restrictions are not documented.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state job guarantee is not in their documented platforms; they accept markets and keep welfare systems.

democratic-peace.rationale: International-relations theory is not engaged by these parties.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: They stress probity and competent governance; anarchist-type view is out of frame.

non-intervention.rationale: Strict non-intervention is not a documented stance.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not documented, since they avoid class-based politics.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy politics belongs to the far right, which sources set apart from this family.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency is a valence issue for these parties.

local-production.rationale: Localism in production is not documented; they emphasise growth.

informal-organisation.rationale: They build centralised, leader-led electoral organisations.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Euroscepticism suggests mild leaning but no source states it.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not documented for this family.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not relevant; they accept private property in general.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-communism as a doctrine is not documented; their anti-establishment target is mainstream parties.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Business-style technocrats are open to mixed provision; inferred from market acceptance and kept welfare systems.

religion-illusion.rationale: Atheist critique of religion is not part of their positions.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: They accept capitalism and value growth.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of household work is not documented.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not documented.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Utopian communalism is alien to them.

majority-settlement.rationale: Ethnic engineering is alien to non-nativist centrists.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: They accept the market economy; though 'beyond left and right', they are not third-way utopians.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical or religious land claims are not documented for them.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Holocaust denial belongs to the extremism that Hanley and Sikk say these parties lack.

suppress-opposition.rationale: They say they do not reject pluralism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A militant-Islamist doctrine well outside this secular, non-extremist family.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Some promote direct democracy; empowering citizens is a stated aim.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Centrist populism is defined as a non-ideological approach that claims to go beyond left and right, and valence populists are explicitly not placeable on the left-right spectrum; Macron's movement sought to transcend party boundaries.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Lacks the nativism of the far right; but culturally cautious ones differ.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: They claim authority from the people.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment-law detail is not documented for them.

social-market-economy.rationale: They accept market economy and keep existing welfare systems, which matches a market economy with social protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Non-radical and not documented as pacifist.

rich-first.rationale: Unequal-growth strategies are not documented in the sources.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Bloc neutrality is not documented; Macron-type centrists are firmly pro-alliance, others less so.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Anti-establishment; though a monarch led one party, dynastic leadership is not an aim.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Positions on IMF conditionality are not documented, and parties differ.

property-franchise.rationale: They claim to speak for all ordinary people.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A Marxist critique of press ownership not found in these parties' sources.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Their criticism of rule-of-law constraints stands against other commitments to probity.

racial-franchise.rationale: Hanley and Sikk set these parties apart from the racism of far-right outsiders and scholars hold that they do not challenge liberal democracy.

online-participation.rationale: Some, such as Italy's Five Star, use online democracy; sources include similar movements as valence populists.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency and anti-corruption claims fit openness.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition-based deliberation is not documented, though citizen empowerment is a stated aim.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is not part of their agenda.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Wealth concentration is not documented; business founders lead several parties.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: LGBT policy is a cultural issue they avoid.

term-limits.rationale: Anti-establishment and anti-entrenchment rhetoric fits term limits; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not documented, though online-democracy parties like Five Star exist in the wider valence family.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential risk is not part of their agenda.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious institutional policy is not documented.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Local voting rights for foreigners are not documented.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy is not documented in the sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: Abolition of intellectual property is a fringe idea; market-accepting parties are unlikely to back it.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is not documented for this family.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign basing is not documented; they are not anti-Western.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Recognition politics are not documented in the sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: No documented view on the source of income legitimacy.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: A gender-theory question outside their agenda.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory debates are not part of these parties' platforms.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cultural-nationalist sequencing is not documented for this family.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology is not part of these secular parties' positions.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology is not part of their positions.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Administrative unification for peoples is not documented.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence from the state is not documented, though pluralism suggests agreement.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A debate within socialism these parties do not engage with.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public ownership of local utilities is not documented; they accept markets but keep welfare systems.

second-chamber.rationale: Parliamentary structure is not documented for this family.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Libertarian municipalism is outside their frame.

family-wage.rationale: Wage-setting norms are not documented; economic policy is blurred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Payments privacy is not documented, and anti-corruption stances point the other way.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online anonymity is not documented in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Personalist philosophy is not documented for them.

spiritual-nature.rationale: A religious-philosophical claim they do not address.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning is not documented for them.

racial-pride.rationale: Race-based identity is not part of their agenda, and they lack the far-right's racial politics.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Linguistic nationhood is not documented; they are only mildly nationalistic.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiratorial nationalism is not a feature.

future-generations.rationale: Intergenerational duty is not a documented theme.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Difference feminism is not part of their documented platforms.

arms-reduction.rationale: Arms control is not documented in the sources.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Open-diplomacy doctrine is not documented, though transparency is a valence theme.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital controls clash with their acceptance of the market economy and EU single market.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Benefit design is not documented beyond keeping existing welfare systems.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Binding fiscal rules are not documented; parties differ in budget attitudes.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Global economic reform for developing states is not documented.

smash-state-machine.rationale: They want a cleaner state, not its smashing.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: A voluntarist-socialist idea not found in the sources.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student debt is not documented for this family.

internal-colonialism.rationale: A regionalist theory not discussed for these parties.

shared-human-nature.rationale: A philosophical anthropology claim they do not address.

public-service-media.rationale: Public media funding is not documented, and their anti-establishment stance may clash with it.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminist structural analysis is not part of their platforms, which avoid socio-cultural questions.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral censorship is not documented, and they are not culturally conservative.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Colonial economic policy is irrelevant to modern centrist populists.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The family avoids doctrine and takes no religious stance, so no answer follows from its principles.

farm-price-support.rationale: Centrist populists accept the market economy and existing welfare systems without a farm programme; inferred from that and left neutral.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The family is not defined by foreign or defence doctrine; inferred as neutral.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: these parties claim to speak for ordinary people across classes rather than a single class, so a separate workers' party runs against their catch-all pitch.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the family's competence-and-probity moderate mainstream stance, which would not defend the practice; the sources do not discuss it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: these parties accept existing legal and EU-aligned norms in which women have equal property rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not an issue for the family; no stance follows from its principles.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: reform-minded centrist parties work within ordinary regulatory states and do not favour a private-suit alternative to agencies.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from their stress on elected, accountable representation, with no formal role for traditional leaders.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The family has no distinctive environmental doctrine; it avoids trading off values in this way.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Law-and-order positions vary across the family; some, such as GERB, are tough on crime while others are not.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The family is less nativist than right-wing populism but not liberal-multicultural; inferred as split.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Centrist populists avoid doctrine on labour relations and accept the existing market and welfare settings; nothing in the sources addresses union dues, so adherents are inferred as split.

voter-id.rationale: Their focus is corruption and election probity, which could favour ID checks, but the sources give no position and the family avoids culture-war issues; inferred as split.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The family is non-nativist and avoids religious politics, so mild support for equal legal treatment of religious streams is inferred; the sources never discuss it.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: They criticise liberal checks only moderately and campaign on cleaner, more responsive elections, which fits a procedural view of democracy; inferred, not stated.

premarital-sex.rationale: The family is not socially conservative and avoids moral campaigns, so acceptance is inferred; the sources do not mention sexual morality.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Their reformist, pro-EU and anti-corruption stance suggests discomfort with shutdowns, but the sources never discuss them; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: They accept existing welfare systems rather than replacing them, so a wholesale swap to a cash payment is inferred as unlikely to be backed.

women-suffrage.rationale: These are modern electoral parties competing in liberal democracies with equal suffrage, which they do not question; the sources do not discuss it directly. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Non-ideological and non-secularist, the family takes no anti-religious line; disagreement is inferred from that absence.

race-social-construct.rationale: Sources note the absence of far-right racism in the family, so adherents would not hold biological views of race, though they do not address the claim.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Mainstream centrist, EU-aligned reformers generally keep existing equality bodies; this is inferred, with no position stated in the sources.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the family avoids doctrine on property.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the family's anti-corruption, pro-EU, rule-of-law image; international courts are not discussed in its sources.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from its secular, non-ideological technocratic style; religion is not addressed.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed by the family; no basis for inference.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The family accepts the market economy and existing welfare systems and rejects ideological projects; inferred from that.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from its anti-establishment appeal to direct popular choice over party-controlled selection; not discussed explicitly.

national-church-status.rationale: Not addressed by the family; adherents are split by country.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from its weaker commitment to minority claims and its non-ideological, majority-oriented appeal.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed by the family; no basis for inference.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed by the family; no basis for inference.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from its focus on rising living standards; lifestyle is not addressed.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed by the family; no basis for inference.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed by the family; adherents are split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: the family is less nationalist than right-wing populism, and parties differ on homeland rhetoric.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: the family is moderate on democratic checks and lacks the far-right's punitive bent, so extrajudicial killing is rejected.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred: parties differ, with pro-EU Macron-style and Eurosceptic ANO-style strands.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred: the family is less nationalist and nativist, so kin-minority support is not a defining concern.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the family avoids doctrine and does not discuss resource ownership.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred: it accepts the market economy and existing liberal order, but states no self-ownership doctrine.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from a cost-of-living, living-standards focus and ANO's mixed economic measures; not stated as a rule.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: the family accepts existing welfare systems without a stance on targeting.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the family attacks mainstream parties and relies on personalistic outsider leaders, though it only moderately criticises liberal checks.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Anti-corruption is the family's core appeal, and favouritism toward connected businesses is the corruption it attacks.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred: a non-ideological, less identity-driven family would keep politics non-denominational.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: the family avoids doctrine on tradition versus modernity.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred: the family is socially moderate and lacks the far-right's traditionalism.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: parties differ, with business-friendly ANO and a pro-EU strand.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred: the family has no distributive theory and blurs economic stances.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred: economic positions are blurred and the sources do not mention this tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: the family lacks far-right racism but does not address racial advancement, so this is split.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: the family is technocratic and legalistic about procedure but gives no view on natural law.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred: not addressed; the family is non-doctrinal on economics.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred: the family is mostly pro-EU or mildly Eurosceptic without a multipolar doctrine.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: the family accepts the market economy and carries no labour-value theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: it is less nationalist, so patriotism is not tied to a worker-focused politics.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: it rejects left-right framing, so it takes no side on this.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The family accepts the market economy and avoids ideology, so it does not support communist-party rule.

missingStatements.text: Government ministries should be run by non-political experts or business managers rather than by career politicians.
missingStatements.rationale: Technocratic centrist populists such as Czech ANO present business-style, expert-run government as their remedy for the established parties.

notes: The family is heterogeneous: Macron-style pro-EU centrists and Eurosceptic ANO-type parties diverge on the EU and currency, and some parties (Fidesz, PiS) later became right-wing populist. Answers on culture, religion and foreign policy are mostly inferred because these parties deliberately avoid taking positions.
